column3: the Beta-Bernoulli expected-loss comparison P(theta_b > theta_a) can be evaluated in bounded fixed-point integer arithmetic by iterating its exact term recurrence at a large scale, so no arbitrary-precision rationals are needed
column4: DISPROVEN BY MEASUREMENT, and the failure is silent rather than loud. A u128 fixed-point implementation at scale 1e24 returns exactly 0 ppm for ordinary parameter sizes -- not an inaccurate answer but a confidently wrong one, and 0 ppm reads as the candidate policy NEVER beats the fallback, which would pin a controller to its fallback permanently while looking like evidence. The closed form and its recurrence are exact and correct; it is the fixed-point EVALUATION that fails. Recorded because the approach is the obvious one and looks sound: the recurrence is factorial-free, every factor is a small rational, and nothing in it suggests underflow.
column5: The series spans more dynamic range than any fixed scale can hold. Measured T0 against the exact rational value: Beta(3,4) vs Beta(5,2) gives T0=3.571e-01; Beta(101,101) vs Beta(151,51) gives 7.166e-14; Beta(501,501) vs Beta(601,401) gives 2.955e-96; Beta(1001,1001) vs Beta(1501,501) gives 1.169e-129. The PEAK term is ~1e-2 in every case, so the series starts negligibly small and grows, spanning ~127 orders of magnitude between first term and peak while u128 offers ~38 decimal digits. T0 truncates to 0 at scale 1e24 and every later term is 0*ratio=0. Exact-rational evaluation agrees with numerical integration on four parameter sets including the symmetric control Beta(2,2) vs Beta(3,3) = 500000 ppm exactly, so the mathematics is not in question.
